items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: go across the street, next to Jack Dempsey's hang out there and drink before we go to Harlem

ctx.x: I had a cymbal -- They had a band called the California Ramblers, a big white band, and the drummer was Stanley somebody. They were a good band, they could play, big band, so we had a fire. That was the ritual--the fire, when a holiday come up like the -- what's that day -- Palm Sunday or something, the boss Leo Bernstein come up and say, "hey

you all take your horns home, we're going to have an accident down there tonight. Sonny, leave them drums just like they are." I'd take the cymbals and put them in the piano and pull the lid down, because cymbals ain't going to burn. Man, now remember this is on 49th and Broadway. Man, that morning we get off and go across the street, next to Jack Dempsey's hang out there and drink before we go to Harlem, I was standing up there drinking with some boys in our gang, and get to lollygagging, here come the fire…

I swear before God, I ain't exaggerating and lying, that was New York. See, business would get slack. What do you call that. Sort of a two-three week holiday, slow or something like that, we'd have a fire over there. Next day, the insurance people would be rebuilding the club and the boss would tell me, "Sonny, go get a new set of drums."
